title: Exile Oracle: patch -> price impact dataset (PoE 2 0.1-0.5.5h)

rules.trigger_pattern: 'now (also) drops / has a chance to drop / always drops', 'increased the drop rate', 'X% more', 'more common' + a named exchange item
rules.basis: sourced: hand-reviewed lines, GGG exchange history (measured)

examples.line: Fixed a bug where the Hinekora's Lock runic inscription reward was guaranteed in some circumstances. As a result, this outcome has been re-enabled.
Increased the amount of Exotic Coinage that drops by +50%
Lowered the drop rate of Artificer's Orbs and distributed it to Lesser Jeweller's Orbs.
Conquering the Vessel of Kulemak now has a chance to drop Ancient Jawbones, Ancient Ribs and Ancient Collarbones.
Overall past level 52 you will now drop more Greater Runes than currently, but Lesser Runes and Runes will no longer drop.
Increased the drop rate of Regal Orbs.
Styrn, Fallen Knight of Aldur in the Tomb of the Fallen Knight now always drops an Expedition Logbook.
Breach splinter drop rates have been increased by +50%.
Significantly increased the drop rate of Gemcutter's Prisms.
Fixed an issue where The Immured Fury wouldn't spawn.

A number of Maps now have 50% more chance to contain Essences.
Breach hands now can drop splinters at all levels. This amount starts low and increases with area level, similar to splinter drops from monsters.

Omen of Sinistral Erasure, Omen of Dextral Erasure, Omen of Sinistral Annulment, Omen of Dextral Annulment, Omen of the Blessed and Omen of Sanctification can now generate in Rituals in level 79 and above instead of 80 a
Increased the amount of Simulacrum Splinters found in Maps by 20%.

Adjusted the appearance of all Omens, the same number of Omens appear but which omens they are has been adjusted heavily to have the rare, and more powerful ones appear more frequently. The rarest ones should appear six-
Delirium splinter drop rates have been increased by +80%.
The Twisted Domain now drops significantly more Catalysts on average.

rules.trigger_pattern: 'no longer drops', 'lowered the drop rate', 'rarer' + a named exchange item
rules.basis: sourced: hand-reviewed lines, GGG exchange history (measured)

examples.line: Lowered the drop rate of Chaos Orbs and distributed it amongst the other more valued Currency Items (Like Regal Orbs, Exalted Orbs).
Lesser Runes no longer drop past level 31.
Lowered the drop rate of Artificer's Orbs and distributed it to Lesser Jeweller's Orbs.
Soul Cores are no longer able to drop outside of the Temple of Chaos.

rules.trigger_pattern: diminishing returns, caps, 'reduced the rewards/number of chests', exploit/infinite/duplicate fixes on a farm

Fixed a bug where Additional Different Catalyst Chance on the Genesis Tree was not respecting choices from Ignorant to Power.
Halved the chances of finding Uromoti's Medallion (Bonus Room) and Hayoxi's Medallion (Reroll Reward Room).
Fixed Amanamu's Void monster modifier dropping multiple additional Omens, instead of just 1.
Players will no longer be able to get Energised Crystals from areas they significantly over-level.

rules.trigger_pattern: 'greatly improved', 'doubled the runs', 'increased item rarity per depth' for a mechanic
rules.basis: sourced: hand-reviewed lines, GGG exchange history (measured)

examples.line: Map Areas now grant additional Energized Crystals, scaling with Map Tier and number of Modifiers. This results in double the number of temple runs you can do when using 6-mod Tier 15 maps.
Increased the amount of Item Rarity per depth in Delirium encounters. It increases to approximately 2.5 times what it was before.
Grand Expedition chests have been greatly improved:

rules.trigger_pattern: a change to how rewarding a mechanic is, read for its ENTRY item (Logbook, Simulacrum, Breachstone)
rules.affected_group: the entry item (up if the farm got better, down if worse)
rules.typical_move_note: in the EXPECTED direction of each case (+ = moved as predicted)
rules.basis: sourced: hand-reviewed lines, GGG exchange history (measured)

examples.line: Grand Expedition chests have been greatly improved:

The Delirious percentage scaling with waves in Simulacrum has been reduced. Each wave now adds 5% Delirious (previously 10%), up to a maximum of 75% at Difficulty zero (previously 100%), and 115% at Difficulty 4 (previou
Simulacrums now start at 100% Delirious, scaling up to 200%. This was previously intended to be 0% scaling up to 100%, but was actually not working at all.
Every section of the Ocean revealed by an Expedition Logbook is now guaranteed to contain at least one Grand Expedition.

reading_checklist.look_for: 'now (also) drops / has a chance to drop / can now be found' + an exchange item
reading_checklist.why: New source = more supply. Strongest single signal in PoE 2 so far (0.5.3 Kulemak bones).
reading_checklist.action: Sell that item before the patch deploys or within the first hours; do not buy the dip on day 1, the floor came after 3-7 days.

reading_checklist.look_for: 'no longer drops / removed from / only drops from' + an item
reading_checklist.why: Supply cut; existing stock becomes scarcer.
reading_checklist.action: Hold or buy before deploy if the item still has a use; check that the use was not removed in the same notes.

reading_checklist.look_for: Explicit drop-rate numbers ('X% more common', 'doubled', 'halved') for currency
reading_checklist.why: Divine / Exalted / Chaos ratio changes move every price in the league.
reading_checklist.action: Re-price in Divine on the day; for a Divine buff expect Div:Ex to rise more slowly, not fall outright.

reading_checklist.look_for: A farm strategy nerf: diminishing returns, caps, 'reduced rewards', exploit fixes ('could be rerolled infinitely', 'duplicated')
reading_checklist.why: The farm's outputs get scarcer; its inputs (tablets, fragments, waystones, medallions) lose demand.
reading_checklist.action: Hold the outputs a few days; sell the farm's inputs immediately.

reading_checklist.look_for: A mechanic reward buff ('greatly improved', 'doubled the number of chests', 'improve the rewards ... more significantly')
reading_checklist.why: That mechanic's outputs get more common; its entry items (fragments, logbooks, splinters) get more demand.
reading_checklist.action: Sell the outputs you hold; buy the mechanic's entry items early.

reading_checklist.look_for: Crafting: a new omen/currency, 'can now be used on', 'no longer works with', inverted or reworked omens
reading_checklist.why: Demand shock for the currency; also for the items it replaces.
reading_checklist.action: Expect the largest % moves on thin, expensive omens; wait 24 h for the first spike to settle before buying.

reading_checklist.look_for: Socketables: soul core / rune / talisman stat changes
reading_checklist.why: The item's use value changes directly.
reading_checklist.action: Buff: buy the cheap ones before deploy. Nerf: sell.

reading_checklist.why: Second order: the build's lineage supports, key uniques and bases move, not exchange currency.
reading_checklist.action: List the 2-3 uniques and lineage gems each buffed build needs (from your own vault / guides, never the builds API) and price-check them on day 0 and day 3.

reading_checklist.look_for: Unique item changes ('The X Unique Y now ...')
reading_checklist.why: Direct demand change for one unique.
reading_checklist.action: Check whether old copies keep the old stats (legacy) before selling or buying.

reading_checklist.look_for: Vendor / recipe / Currency Exchange listing changes
reading_checklist.why: Can create a price floor or ceiling (gold cost, vendor recipe) or make an item tradeable for the first time.
reading_checklist.action: An item newly added to the exchange often re-prices sharply in 24 h as listings consolidate.

reading_checklist.look_for: Where in the league the patch lands (league day)
reading_checklist.why: Days 0-14 have huge normal drift (Ex loses 50% vs Div in week 1). The patch effect must be read net of that drift.
reading_checklist.action: Compare with the same-group drift (rules.py gives the net move), not the raw chart.

reading_checklist.look_for: For 1.0 itself: the content-update post before launch
reading_checklist.why: Launch-day prices come from a fresh economy, so pre-1.0 prices don't carry over; the notes tell you which groups will be abundant or scarce at launch.
reading_checklist.action: Use market-trends.md phase patterns for launch week; use this rulebook for the hotfixes from day 1 on.

not_verified: Deploy time vs post time: forum post time is used as the event time. Most GGG patch posts go up at deployment, but some (0.4.0d, 0.1.1) had previews hours or days earlier on Steam.
0.1 (Early Access, Standard league) has no cross-league phase control, and its early Div:Ex digests look odd (about 3.6 Ex per Div on 2024-12-13). Treat 0.1 cases as low quality.

Unique items: poe.ninja item history reaches back only about 120 days (Runes of Aldur from about 2026-07-25, Forbidden Rites). Only 3 unique cases exist in that window, all minor bug fixes, so no unique rule is measured.
Skill / ascendancy second-order effects (buffed skill -> key uniques and lineage gems) could not be measured: there is no unique history for 0.1-0.5.4, and the builds API is off limits.
Single-hour exchange prices for thin items are noisy (random single items move a median 24% / 38% / 49% vs drift over 24 h / 72 h / 7 d). Most single-item cases are not beyond the placebo band.
Patches often arrive in clusters (0.4.0c had 26 hotfixes). 7-day windows often contain later patches; the 0.5.2 -> 0.5.3 Transcendent Alloy flip is an example.

GGG reacts to the market (selection): a farm is usually nerfed because its outputs were crashing or the exploit was spreading, so the before-trend is part of the story (pre7 is stored for every case).
Expected directions were set by hand before looking at the result, but the curated list itself is my judgement of which lines matter (52 lines); a different reader could pick differently.
The automated classifier rows are noisy: it tags many lines that move nothing, and its mechanic -> item mapping is coarse.
Cross-league phase control uses only 2 comparison leagues and single hours, and league-specific items (Runes of Aldur Verisium, Fate of the Vaal temple currency) often have no counterpart.
